chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Indeed, in the Torah it is written:

O Moses, indeed I created you, formed you, and strengthened you, and I commanded you to obey Me, and I prohibited you from disobeying Me. So if you obey Me, I will help you in obeying Me. And if you disobey Me, I will not help you in disobeying Me.
O Moses, to Me belongs the grace upon you in your obedience to Me, and to Me belongs the proof against you in your disobedience to Me.

key_terms.اصْطَنَعْتُكَ: I formed/chose you (istana'tuka) - implies special selection and careful formation, beyond mere creation
key_terms.التَّوْرَاة: The Torah (Tawrah) - the scripture revealed to Prophet Moses, referenced here as containing God's direct address
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The proof/argument (al-hujjah) - God's established proof against the disobedient, a key concept in Shia theology
key_terms.الْمِنَّةُ: The grace/favour (al-minnah) - God's benevolent grace that enables obedience

ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about divine assistance in obedience and disobedience according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq preserves a passage attributed to the Torah in which God directly addresses Prophet Moses (Musa). God reminds Moses that He created, formed, and strengthened him, then commanded obedience and forbade disobedience. The core theological teaching is reciprocal: obedience earns divine assistance in further obedience, while disobedience results in withdrawal of that assistance. The passage concludes with two powerful declarations: that God's grace is manifest in the servant's obedience, and God's proof (hujjah) is established against the servant through disobedience. This reflects the Shia theological position on divine justice (adl) -- God enables but does not compel, and the servant's choices establish either grace or accountability. Imam al-Baqir likely cited this Torah passage to illustrate that these principles of divine justice are universal across revealed scriptures.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from Hisham b. Salim from Habib al-Sijistani from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as).
He said: Surely, in the Torah, it is written:

O Musa! Surely, I created you, formed you, and strengthened you. I ordered you to obey Me and I prohibited you from disobeying Me. If you obey Me, I will support you in obeying Me, but if you disobey Me, I will not support you in disobeying Me.
O Musa! It is upon Me to be graceful to you in your obedience to Me, but the argument against you is in My favour if you disobey Me.
